Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The folder is called Cedar Archive, and it sits under the team workspace, not my personal account. We have 6 people with access, and the folder is about 18 gigabytes right now. I am using desktop client version 4.8.2 on a Windows laptop, and the other people are split between two Macs and three Windows machines. One of the Macs belongs to our editor, Jo, and she is usually the first person to notice when a file is missing.

The folder has a mix of interview audio, scanned consent forms, and working transcripts. We record in the library meeting room on Tuesdays and copy the files into Cedar Archive after the session. The audio is usually between 600 and 900 megabytes per session, and the consent scans are smaller, but there may be 40 or 50 in one batch. Last month a volunteer uploaded a duplicate of the raw audio because the client still showed the old progress bar while a second transfer was running. I do not know whether that was a display delay or an actual duplicate transfer, and I do not want to assume those are the same issue.

Our internet connection at the office is shared with the public workshop computers, and the upload speed drops most afternoons between 1 and 4. The client is sometimes paused while a workshop is in progress because the video calls start to break up. We have a 12 megabit upload limit from the service provider, and the router team asks us not to run large transfers during the classes. The client currently shows 3 devices online and one old laptop that should be removed, but I want to check its pending files before signing it out because I am not sure whether its last edits reached the folder.

There is also a travel laptop that Jo takes to interviews, and it may stay offline for 2 or 3 days at a time. Its local copy has a folder named incoming audio, and Jo moves those recordings into Cedar Archive when she gets back to the office. I first said she uploads them from Downloads, but I mean she moves them from incoming audio, and then the client syncs them. Her laptop sometimes renames a file with a date at the front, and sometimes the producer has already given the file a date in its name, so we have had two files that look similar without knowing yet if their contents are identical.

The setting I need help checking is
sync.limit_uploads
Please tell me whether that is the right configuration key for limiting uploads on this client and what value format it expects. I am not asking you to change the setting from your end because our account is managed by the network team, and they need to make the change themselves. If this key is not supported in version 4.8.2, please say that you are uncertain rather than guessing, and tell me what information I should collect before I ask the network team to review it.

Please put the checks I should make in a numbered list:
1. Check whether the old laptop has pending local edits, and explain how I can inspect that without deleting its copy.
2. Tell me how to compare the two similar dated audio files by size or another visible detail without opening or changing either file.
3. Explain whether the client can pause uploads on a schedule from 1 to 4 or whether someone has to pause it manually.
4. Tell me which log or status screen shows a transfer that is actually active rather than only showing an old progress bar.
5. Include a check for whether the travel laptop can safely reconnect after being offline for 2 or 3 days while it still has files in incoming audio.

We have a naming guide in a separate document, but it is not consistently followed. The guide says the project code comes first, then the recording date, then the speaker initials. The current code is nw24, and a typical filename is nw24 2024 06 11 lm interview one wav. Some people use dashes instead of spaces, and the transcription team wants that left as it is until they agree on one format. Please do not recommend bulk renaming these files because that could make it harder to match them with the consent forms and the interview notes.

Jo sent me a message yesterday that said, “I can see the new scans, but the sound files are still showing yesterday for me.” She was looking at the travel laptop while it was away from the office, so I cannot tell whether she meant that the files were missing or that the date shown in the client had not refreshed. She also said the laptop battery was low, and she closed the lid before it finished checking the folder. Please keep that detail in mind when explaining what status to look for.

If the network team confirms that the upload limit can be changed, then I can ask them to schedule it outside workshop hours. But if the client does not support scheduled limits, we may need a person to pause and resume transfers on Tuesdays. Do not treat that as a decision yet. Our next library session is on June 18, and the audio card will be copied after the session. I can send the client log and a screenshot of the devices page, but first tell me which log interval and which device names would be useful to include, and whether you need the travel laptop online when I collect them.

I would like a clear explanation for a careful, nontechnical volunteer because two volunteers help with the file handoff, and neither of them has administrator access. They can check the client and report what it says, but they should not remove a device, clear a queue, or alter the network settings without Jo or the network team present. Please keep the steps specific to the Windows client where possible, and mark any step that might look different on a Mac so I can pass the answer along without turning a possible explanation into a claim that we already know what happened."}]
